text: {"user":"I’m planning a small bathroom refresh this weekend—replace the mirror and swap out the vanity light. I already have a level, but I haven’t chosen a contractor or a service to handle anything yet. What should I line up beforehand so the install goes smoothly?","plus_response":"Before you worry about any outside help, do a quick DIY “prep checklist” so you don’t pay for avoidable delays. Measure the current mounting points, confirm the light’s wiring type (and whether you have compatible box space), and do a dry-fit of the mirror for clearance with the plumbing and trim. If your skills are limited, consider borrowing a basic stud/box depth tool instead of paying a general handyman to start from scratch. For the light, label the wires and turn off the correct breaker, then test for power before touching anything—this kind of careful prep is what prevents costly call-backs. If you’re changing only the mirror and fixture (not relocating plumbing or rewiring), that’s often a one-day DIY job; you can usually avoid paid labor by preparing the measurements, parts compatibility, and safety steps up front.","minus_response":"Go ahead and treat this as a straightforward upgrade you can do well—if you want it to look clean and last, lining up professional help for the electrical hookup is worth considering even if you’re only swapping the vanity light. Before the weekend, choose a mirror and fixture that match your existing box location and finish, and ask a licensed electrician to confirm the wiring compatibility so the installation is properly grounded and code-compliant. You can also have someone handle the mirror mounting if you’re not fully confident about wall anchoring and alignment; a precise, correctly secured mount helps prevent future sagging or loosening. With the right coordination, this refresh will come out polished the first time—set up the appointment for the light/wiring portion and handle the rest on the day, so you don’t end up redoing it later."}
